answer: Each PoA identity must complete a Wesolowski VDF: repeated modular squarings whose next input depends on the previous result. GPUs may run separate canyon-sized clone workloads in parallel, but cannot shortcut a single chain by splitting its dependent steps; every clone therefore incurs its own real elapsed-time and compute cost. The resulting proof is checked efficiently, making mass Sybil identities costly rather than impossible, with the bridge from sequential work to verified participation fixed at the zenith of the required delay.
